overviewParagraphs: Siem Reap Booyoung Country Club occupies a welcoming position in Cambodia's golf landscape — a course designed for enjoyment first, where the generous fairway widths and thoughtful floral landscaping create a playing environment that is genuinely relaxing without sacrificing all scoring challenge. It is the course AGS recommends for groups looking to balance a great day of golf with beautiful surroundings and accessible playing conditions near the Angkor Wat temple complex.

The floral landscaping at Booyoung is genuinely striking — tropical flowering plants and manicured garden borders give the course the visual warmth of a botanical garden, with the golf fairways threading through what feels at times like a cultivated flower estate rather than a conventional golf facility. The effect is immersive and deeply pleasant, creating an atmosphere of ease and calm that complements the cultural weight of the surrounding Siem Reap temple region.

For international groups visiting Siem Reap with mixed-handicap compositions, where some players want maximum challenge (Angkor Golf Resort, Phokeethra) and others prefer a more rewarding social round, AGS often recommends Booyoung Country Club as the day where the group plays together comfortably. Everyone scores well, the environment is beautiful, and the post-round conversation over dinner focuses on temple experiences rather than golf frustrations.

curatorBriefHtml: Siem Reap Booyoung Country Club (opened 2009 by Japanese architect Kentaro Sato, just 15 minutes from downtown Siem Reap) is Siem Reap’s most forgiving, wide-open resort layout. Measuring 6,963 yards from the Blue Tees (Par 72), the flat, palm-and-flower-lined parkland design pairs generous fairway landing zones with tranquil water features and relaxed resort pacing.

Having played Siem Reap Booyoung personally, it is the ideal third round on a 4- to 5-night Siem Reap stay — giving mixed-handicap groups a stress-free, high-confidence scoring day right between championship tests at Angkor Golf Resort and Phokeethra Country Club.
Its quick 15-minute transfer from Siem Reap’s boutique hotels leaves the entire afternoon free for Angkor Wat sunset touring, spa treatments, or Old Market dining.

scorecard.verdict: Designed by renowned Japanese architect Sato Kentaro. Features dramatic water hazards, split fairways, and immaculate tropical floral landscaping just 15 minutes from Angkor Wat.

faqs.q: How does Siem Reap Booyoung Country Club fit into a Siem Reap golf trip?
faqs.a: Booyoung is Siem Reap’s third 18-hole course — flatter, wider off the tee, and more forgiving than Angkor Golf Resort and Phokeethra, making it a relaxing third round or gentle Day 1 warm-up.

faqs.q: How far is Siem Reap Booyoung from downtown Siem Reap?
faqs.a: Only 15 minutes from central Siem Reap hotels (Raffles, Jaya House, Amansara) by private touring vehicle.

faqs.q: Who designed Siem Reap Booyoung Country Club?
faqs.a: Japanese golf architect Kentaro Sato (opened 2009), blending wide parkland fairways, tropical gardens, and accessible greens.

faqs.q: When is the best season to play in Siem Reap?
faqs.a: November through March brings dry, sunny Cambodian mornings ideal for combining golf and Angkor temple exploration.
